services.name: Users
services.description: Needed to represent external clients (browsers, mobile apps, IoT) generating request traffic and latency benchmarks for testing.

services.name: Route 53

rules.description: Route 53 can resolve to API Gateway.

services.description: Needed to resolve user-friendly domains (e.g. app.com) into AWS resource endpoints like CloudFront or Application Load Balancers.

services.name: CloudFront

rules.description: CloudFront can use S3 as an origin.
CloudFront can use ALB as an origin.
CloudFront queries WAF for threat detection.

services.description: Needed to cache static assets close to users, dramatically reducing latency, bandwidth costs, and load on origin servers.

services.name: API Gateway

rules.description: API Gateway can integrate directly with SQS.
API Gateway can integrate directly with SNS.
API Gateway can start Step Function workflows.
API Gateway can route HTTP to Load Balancers.
API Gateway can route traffic directly to EC2 instances.
API Gateway can route to ECS.
API Gateway emits logs and metrics to CloudWatch.
API Gateway routes to EKS clusters.

services.description: Needed as a secure, unified entry point to route HTTP API requests to backend services like Lambda, handling auth and traffic rates.

services.name: ELB / ALB

rules.description: Load Balancers route traffic to EC2 targets.
Load Balancers route traffic to ECS services.
ALB distributes traffic to EKS pods.
ALB routes traffic to App Runner.

services.description: Needed to distribute HTTP traffic across multiple compute targets, ensuring high availability and handling load scaling.

services.name: Lambda

rules.description: Lambda can send messages to SQS.
Lambda can call other APIs via Gateway.
LAMBDA pulls container package images from ECR.
Lambda functions connect to VPC endpoints via PrivateLink.

services.description: Needed to execute backend business logic serverlessly on an event-driven basis, paying only for the exact milliseconds consumed.

services.name: EC2

rules.description: EC2 instances pull docker images from ECR.
EC2 instances connect to VPC endpoints via PrivateLink.

services.description: Needed when you require full OS-level control, custom software configurations, or long-running stateful services that run continuously.

services.name: ECS

rules.description: ECS pulls container images from ECR.
ECS tasks connect to VPC endpoints via PrivateLink.

services.description: Needed to deploy containerized microservices (Docker) at scale on Fargate serverless compute, bypassing virtual machine management.

services.name: SQS
services.description: Needed to buffer and queue requests asynchronously, decoupling services so spikes in traffic do not cause downstream outages.

services.name: SNS

rules.description: SNS can fan out to SQS.
SNS can integrate with CloudWatch for metrics and events.
SNS emits telemetry to observability services.
SNS can trigger AWS Batch jobs via event notifications.

services.description: Needed to broadcast notification events to multiple subscribers (fan-out pattern) asynchronously without hardcoding service linkages.

services.name: S3

rules.description: S3 can be an origin for CloudFront.
S3 emits usage and performance metrics to CloudWatch.

services.description: Needed as a highly durable, cheap, and scalable object store for static assets, media uploads, database backups, and data logs.

services.name: RDS
services.description: Needed for structured SQL data storage supporting ACID transactions, automated backups, and read replicas for high-concurrency scaling.

services.name: DynamoDB

rules.description: DynamoDB emits operational metrics to CloudWatch.

services.description: Needed as a NoSQL database that delivers predictable single-digit millisecond latency at any scale, supporting high-throughput key-value APIs.

services.name: ElastiCache
services.description: Needed as an in-memory database cache to store frequent queries, reducing database load and speeding up reads to microseconds.

services.name: CloudWatch

rules.description: CloudWatch Alarms and Events can trigger SNS.

services.description: Needed to collect metrics, logs, and alarms from all AWS resources, enabling automated scaling actions and system monitoring.

services.name: Step Functions

rules.description: Step Functions can send to SQS.
Step Functions can publish to SNS.
Step Functions can call external APIs.

services.description: Needed to coordinate complex multi-service workflows and state machines with built-in retries, branching logic, and error handling.

services.name: VPC

rules.description: VPC uses NAT Gateway for outbound traffic.
VPC uses Security Groups for firewalling.

services.description: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) lets you provision a logically isolated section of the AWS Cloud where you can launch AWS resources in a virtual network.

services.name: IAM
services.description: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) enables you to manage access to AWS services and resources securely.

services.name: Auto Scaling Group

services.name: Security Group

AWS Batch publishes logs and metrics to Amazon CloudWatch.
AWS Batch triggers AWS Lambda after job completion.
AWS Batch provisions EC2 compute environments for job execution.

services.description: AWS Batch enables developers, scientists, and engineers to easily and efficiently run hundreds of thousands of batch computing jobs on AWS.
